Definition: % of used capacity versus total usable space across all tiers.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No monitoring. Alerts only trigger when disks are 100% full.
Level 2 - Developing: Manual checks. Basic alerts set at 90% utilization.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated alerts integrated into ITSM/ticketing system.
Level 5 - Optimized: Dynamic thresholds based on workload and growth rate.

Definition: Predictive analysis of when existing storage will be exhausted.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No forecasting. Storage is bought only when it runs out.
Level 2 - Developing: Spreadsheet-based tracking of historical monthly growth.
Level 3 - Defined: 6-month growth forecast documented and updated quarterly.
Level 4 - Managed: 12-month predictive modeling based on automated trends.
Level 5 - Optimized: 24-month predictive modeling based on automated trends.

Definition: Effectiveness of Deduplication and Compression to save space.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No deduplication. Multiple copies of same data exist.
Level 2 - Developing: Compression enabled on some volumes but not monitored.
Level 3 - Defined: DRR tracked manually. Target ratios set for different tiers.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated reporting on savings from Dedup/Compression.
Level 5 - Optimized: Global deduplication across all sites and cloud tiers.

Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No monitoring. Manual check of Storage Volumes during slow-downs.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic metrics available but not reviewed regularly.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated alerts for latency spikes & anomalies.
Level 5 - Optimized: Read and Write IOPS are optimized across all storage.

Level 1 - Ad Hoc: All data on one tier. No performance SLAs.
Level 2 - Developing: Static tiers (SSD vs HDD) assigned manually.
Level 3 - Defined: Tiers defined by business impact & app needs.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated tiering. Data moves based on hot/cold use.

Definition: Keep the Storage Firmware updated based on compatibility with SAN and Servers
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No tracking. Arrays running various random versions.
Level 2 - Developing: Manual inventory list. Updates only during outages.
Level 3 - Defined: N-1 or N-2 policy defined. Annual update cycle.
Level 4 - Managed: Check periodically and update based on Advisory from OEM
Level 5 - Optimized: Managing the Storage firmware compatibility based on SAN and Server Firmware.

Level 2 - Developing: Manual updates. Requires full system downtime.
Level 3 - Defined: Check periodically and update based on Advisories from Storage OEMs
Level 4 - Managed: SLA-driven patching, Security fixes within 30 days.
Level 5 - Optimized: SLA-driven patching. CVE Security fixes within 7 days.

Definition: % of workloads (VMs, DBs, Files) covered by Backup policies
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Critical systems not configured in Backup
Level 3 - Defined: Backup policies defined and tracked but inconsistently enforced
Level 4 - Managed: >95% workloads configured. Policies enforced via centralized tools
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% workload protection with auto-discovery and policy-based assignment.

Definition: % of successful backup jobs over total scheduled jobs.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic logs available but no tracking.
Level 3 - Defined: Success rate tracked. Failures reviewed manually.
Level 4 - Managed: >95% success rate. Alerts configured for failures.
Level 5 - Optimized: >99% success rate. Auto-remediation and retry mechanism.

Definition: Adherence to defined backup schedules and SLAs.
Frequency and effectiveness of validating the backups that can be restored successfully.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No restore testing performed, recovery success is unknown until failure occurs.
Level 2 - Developing: Occasional/manual restore tests for a few critical systems, no documentation or consistency
Level 3 - Defined: Restore testing is scheduled (e.g. quarterly/annual for key systems). Results are documented.
Level 4 - Managed: Regular restore testing across critical workloads with defined SLAs, results tracked and reviewed.
Level 5 - Optimized: Comprehensive restore testing covering critical workloads, integrated into DR drills with audit and compliance reporting.

Definition: Encryption of backup data at rest and in transit to prevent unauthorized access
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Backups are stored without encryption. Data is accessible in plain format
Level 2 - Developing: Encryption is enabled for some backups but not consistently across all workloads.
Level 3 - Defined: Encryption is standardized for backups but key management is basic or manually handled.
Level 4 - Managed: Encryption is enforced for all backups, centralized key management with controlled access is implemented
Level 5 - Optimized: Encryption is fully enforced with strong key lifecycle management (rotation, audit, restricted access) and compliance alignment.

Definition: Ability to protect backup data from ransomware attacks and ensure clean recovery.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Backups are stored on standard with no isolation, vulnerable to ransomware encryption or deletion.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic security controls in place (access restrictions, antivirus) but backups are still modifiable and exposed.
Level 3 - Defined: Hardened backup repositories with limited access in Cloud/offsite backups.
Level 4 - Managed: Immutable backups enabled with WORM/object lock enabled, separation between backup and production environments.
Level 5 - Optimized: Strict access governance in place with air-gapped backup implemented. Regular recovery testing to ensure clean restore points.
